entries.locator: Lecture beat 1: the deferred Dirac-sea problem and the fermion-boson setup
entries.note: The opening destination and the need to distinguish fermion from boson operator algebra are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 2: two-particle position slots and symmetric bosonic exchange
entries.note: The two creation-operator ordering and bosonic exchange rule are retained before the fermionic contrast.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 3: fermionic exchange and the creation-operator anti-commutator
entries.note: The exchange minus sign is carried into the anti-commutator relation and synchronized board frame.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 4: equal-point anti-commutation and Pauli exclusion
entries.note: The repeated creation operator, factor of two, and nilpotent conclusion are shown in equations, a board frame, and a clean reconstruction.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 5: bosonic commutation relations and the infinite occupation ladder
entries.note: The unrestricted bosonic occupation ladder is retained as the contrast needed for the later sea argument.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 6: the fermionic zero-one ladder and filled-empty symmetry
entries.note: The two-state algebra and formal interchange of creation with annihilation are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 7: the nilpotent-operator question and the promised particle-hole reinterpretation
entries.note: The audience question is retained and a nonzero nilpotent creation operator is explained without contradiction.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 8: the one-dimensional massless right mover and its dispersion
entries.note: The equation H equals P, E equals p, and right-moving group velocity for either sign of p are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 9: adding a left mover, a two-component wavefunction, and alpha
entries.note: The opposite directional components are combined into the two-component massless Hamiltonian.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 10: beta, the one-dimensional mass term, and the squared dispersion
entries.note: The off-diagonal mass coupling and anti-commutator cancellation are developed through H squared.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 11: the physical interpretation of the two directional components
entries.note: The classroom question is retained and the later chirality interpretation is previewed without literal microscopic bouncing.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 12: the three-dimensional alpha vector and its Clifford relations
entries.note: The vector Hamiltonian, diagonal squares, and vanishing cross-term anti-commutators are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 13: the Pauli realization, H equals sigma dot p, energy, and helicity locking
entries.note: All three Pauli matrices and the positive/negative energy eigensectors are shown explicitly.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 14: the classroom exchange about whether spin emerges
entries.note: The response distinguishes emergence within the Dirac construction from a claim that every particle must have spin.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 15: the failed two-by-two mass matrix and the need for four components
entries.note: The absence of a fourth two-by-two matrix anti-commuting with every Pauli matrix is proved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 16: equivalent representations, the full Dirac algebra, and the beta question
entries.note: The minimal four-component algebra and the distinction between beta and a time component of alpha are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 17: the block alpha and beta matrices and the massive Hamiltonian
entries.note: The board representation is paired with complete typeset block matrices and the H squared check.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 18: helicity, chirality, mass mixing, and related audience questions
entries.note: Opposite chiral blocks and their off-diagonal mass coupling are preserved with both classroom exchanges.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 19: the quaternion aside
entries.note: The Pauli/quaternion relation is retained narrowly and distinguished from the full Dirac Clifford algebra.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 20: the spin-energy question and the transition to the physical meaning of alpha
entries.note: The audience exchange is retained before the Heisenberg derivation of velocity.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 21: the Heisenberg-equation derivation that alpha is velocity
entries.note: The commutator calculation from position to the alpha velocity operator is retained step by step.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 22: velocity measurements, nonconservation, zitterbewegung, and classroom questions
entries.note: The sharp component eigenvalues, subluminal expectation, trembling motion, momentum conservation, and four audience questions are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 23: the return to negative energy and the lower-bound requirement for the vacuum
entries.note: The unbounded E equals p spectrum and the energetic definition of a stable vacuum are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 24: filling the fermionic sea, the bosonic contrast, and the modern caveat
entries.note: Exclusion is used to stop the descent, while the failure of a literal bosonic sea and the historical status of the picture are explicit.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 25: the energy ladder, a hole's charge and energy, and the positron
entries.note: The board ladder and clean hole-promotion diagram support the charge and excitation-energy argument.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 26: Dirac's historical prediction, population counting, photon pair creation, and arrows
entries.note: The prediction, classroom population question, charge-flow arrows, and pair-creation qualification are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 27: splitting the field in momentum space and introducing the positron creator
entries.note: The all-momentum integral, sign change, and electron-annihilator/positron-creator split are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 28: one electromagnetic interaction and its emission, annihilation, and pair-creation channels
entries.note: The common local operator, channel equations, kinematic caveat, and board diagrams are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 29: the modern operator reinterpretation of the vacuum
entries.note: The historical sea is replaced directly by positive-energy particle and antiparticle operators.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 30: the condensed-matter Fermi-sea analogy
entries.note: The filled band, promoted electron, and hole analogy are retained together with the limits of the comparison.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 31: questions about bosons, spin, Fermi statistics, and charge counting
entries.note: All four classroom exchanges are retained and disentangle separate field representations and particle labels.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 32: vacuum energy and the cosmological-constant question
entries.note: Bosonic and fermionic zero-point contributions, formal cancellations, subtraction without gravity, and gravitational significance are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 33: the final question about mass and opposite chiralities
entries.note: The lecture closes with the exact off-diagonal mass-coupling statement and no invented summary.
